subsystems.name: Depth lead
subsystems.role: delivers current to a deep brain target and, in newer leads, records the tiny voltages the brain generates nearby.
parts: platinum-iridium contacts (4–8, sometimes segmented for directional steering)

subsystems.name: Implantable pulse generator
subsystems.role: the chest-implanted unit that paces the brain and now also senses it.

subsystems.name: Biomarker detection
subsystems.role: extracts a usable control signal from background brain noise.
parts: band-pass filtering (e.g. 13–35 Hz for Parkinson's beta bursts)

subsystems.name: Control algorithm
subsystems.role: decides when and how much to stimulate, rather than stimulating continuously.

subsystems.name: Clinician programmer and data pipeline
subsystems.role: lets a neurologist set sensing bands, thresholds and stimulation limits, and review recorded trends.
parts: remote follow-up and firmware update channel

subsystems.name: Surgical targeting and imaging
subsystems.role: puts the contacts where the signal and the therapy both work.

buildSteps.title: Pick the target and the patient
buildSteps.detail: High-resolution MRI defines the nucleus (subthalamic nucleus or globus pallidus for movement disorders; subcallosal cingulate or other nodes for psychiatric use), and tractography maps the white-matter pathways each contact will engage.

buildSteps.title: Find a control biomarker
buildSteps.detail: During the implant, signals are recorded from the target while the patient moves or reports symptoms; a feature that tracks symptom severity — classically beta-band bursting in the subthalamic nucleus in Parkinson's disease — becomes the trigger signal.

buildSteps.title: Make the lead
buildSteps.detail: Platinum-iridium rings or segmented contacts are assembled onto a thin polymer shaft over 1.3 mm across, with conductors threaded to a connector at the top and every joint laser-welded and sealed against body fluid.

buildSteps.title: Build the pulse generator
buildSteps.detail: A custom microchip carries the stimulation driver and a low-noise amplifier with an analog-to-digital converter; it is sealed in a welded can with filtered feedthroughs and a rechargeable cell, then sterilised.

buildSteps.title: Implant
buildSteps.detail: Under local or general anaesthesia a burr hole is drilled, the lead is advanced to the target with imaging and often microelectrode guidance, secured at the skull, and an extension wire tunnelled under the skin to the generator in the chest.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the loop
buildSteps.detail: The clinician records the biomarker, sets the sensing band, detection threshold, stimulation amplitude ceilings and the delay between detection and pulse, then tests on and off states against symptoms.

buildSteps.title: Validate against continuous stimulation
buildSteps.detail: Blinded trials compare adaptive with conventional always-on stimulation, measuring motor scores, symptom diaries, side effects and total charge delivered, since the goal is equal or better control with less current.

buildSteps.title: Operate and update
buildSteps.detail: The device runs chronically with artifact rejection active, battery recharge or replacement every few years, and occasional firmware or parameter updates through telemetry.

prerequisites.why: decades of conventional DBS give a proven lead, generator and surgical route to build on.
the beta-band signal in Parkinson's disease is well validated; reliable markers for depression, obsessive-compulsive disorder and other psychiatric conditions are not.
the stimulating pulse is orders of magnitude larger than the microvolt-scale brain signal, so the amplifier must blank and settle fast enough to hear the brain between pulses.
battery size and heat limit how much filtering and classification can run inside the patient rather than on an external computer.
software that changes therapy on its own needs different oversight than a fixed-output stimulator, and few such algorithms have cleared regulators.

pathway.milestone: sensing-capable deep brain stimulators in routine use, and responsive neurostimulation approved for drug-resistant focal epilepsy
pathway.unlocks: a clinical installed base that already records brain signals and can host adaptive control.

pathway.milestone: adaptive stimulation for movement disorders driven by beta-band control reaching routine care
pathway.unlocks: fewer stimulation side effects and longer battery life at equal symptom control.

pathway.milestone: validated biomarkers and closed-loop targets for treatment-resistant depression and obsessive-compulsive disorder
pathway.unlocks: psychiatric use, where conventional fixed DBS results have been mixed and a large sham-controlled depression trial failed its endpoint.

pathway.milestone: multi-channel, multi-biomarker implants that decode mood and motor states continuously
pathway.unlocks: therapy that anticipates symptoms, plus long-term brain recordings for research.
